attributes.body_ja:
「風（ふう）」は何（なに）かの様子（ようす）や状態（じょうたい）、スタイル、方法（ほうほう）を表（あわら）す接尾（せつび）語（ご）で、主（おも）にひらがなで書（か）かれます。

この用法（ようほう）の「ふう」は動詞（どうし）に付（つ）き、またナ形容詞（けいようし）のように活用（かつよう）するので、副詞的（ふくしてき）に使（つか）う場合（ばあい）は「ふうに」となります。これは「(A) のように」や「(A) の方法（ほうほう）で」というような意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）します。

この用法（ようほう）の「ふう」は動詞（どうし）に付（つ）き、またナ形容詞（けいようし）のように活用（かつよう）するので、副詞的（ふくしてき）に使（つか）う場合（ばあい）は「ふうに」となります。これは「(A) のように」や「(A) の方法（ほうほう）で」というような意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）します。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「風（ふう）」にはもともと様式（ようしき）ややり方（かた）、印象（いんしょう）、様子（ようす）などの意味（いみ）がありますが、読（よ）み方（かた）が違（ちが）う同（おな）じ漢字（かんじ）の「風（かぜ）」にもこれと似（に）た使（つか）い方（かた）があります。例（たと）えば「先輩（せんぱい）風（かぜ）を吹（ふ）かす」。「先輩（せんぱい）がその立場（たちば）を利用（りよう）して威張（いば）る」という意味（いみ）で使（つか）われる表現（ひょうげん）で、先輩（せんぱい）から偉（えら）そうに振（ふ）る舞（ま）う様子（ようす）を表（あらわ）しています。
attributes.body:
風（ふう） 'wind', 'air', commonly appearing as kana, is a suffix in Japanese used to indicate that something is in the style, manner, or method of what comes before it.

This use of ふう appears following verbs, and works in the same way as a な-Adjective. This means that it will be followed by に when being used adverbially to further describe something that is being done 'in the way of (A)'.

Also, it is common for ふうに to be used after pre-noun adjectival words such as こんな, そんな, and あんな. This just highlights that something is being done 'like this', 'like that', etc.

Fun-fact

For ease of remembering, coming from the kanji for 風（かぜ） 'wind', ふう can be thought of as similar to English phrases like 'to have an air of (A)', etc. However, this is just a tool for memorization, as the overlap in meaning is not 100%.

attributes.description: ふうに and というふうに
NOUN + 風 as 'NOUN-style, looks like NOUN'
ふう and よう interchangeable?

attributes.body: Both mean in the way of, but differ in usage. ふうに often attaches to demonstratives like こんなふうに (in this way). という風に follows whole phrases, as in すべて分かっているというふうに (as if they knew everything), and can sound slightly more indirect.

attributes.body: Both express resemblance, but with different nuance. かのようだ is used at sentence-end to compare to a hypothetical or exaggerated situation, as in 夢かのようだ (It’s like a dream). ふうに is more neutral and connective, describing manner or appearance, as in こんなふうに書く (Write it like this).

second_relatable.title: ふうに
second_relatable.meaning: ~ way, In a way that suggests, Like ~

attributes.body: 如何 indicates that something depends on conditions, often formal, as in 成否は努力いかんだ (Success depends on effort). ふうに describes the manner or style of something, often casually, as in 彼は変わったふうに話す (He speaks in a strange way).

second_relatable.title: ふうに
second_relatable.meaning: ~ way, In a way that suggests, Like ~

attributes.body: のように・のような and ふうに both express similarity, but with different usage and nuance. のように・のような follows nouns, e.g. 春のような天気 'spring-like weather', and expresses a general comparison. ふうに, on the other hand, typically follows verbs or words like こんな and そんな, implying 'in a way' or 'giving the feel of,' e.g. こんなふうに話す 'to speak in this way'.

second_relatable.title: ふうに
second_relatable.meaning: ~ way, In a way that suggests, Like ~

attributes.body: ふうに and ように・ような both express similarity or comparison, but their nuance differs. ふうに suggests appearing a certain way or having a certain style (literally, a certain 'air'). In contrast, ように・ような implies a more direct comparison or resemblance. Their usage also differs: ふうに is followed by verbs or phrases, while ように connects to phrases and ような to nouns.
